about: Big Man in a Suit of Armor uses two frames from The Avengers (2012). In the top frame Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) glares across at Tony Stark with the subtitle "Take that off and what are you?"; below, Tony (Robert Downey Jr.) stares back with a raised-eyebrow calm, and a white strip under him holds his answer. In the film Tony's reply is a smug list of titles, so the meme has whoever or whatever is being challenged answer with their own list of what they still are without the thing that defines them. It works as a flex, as a roast and as a way to point out that something is nothing without one feature.
origin: The exchange happens during an argument on the S.H.I.E.L.D. helicarrier in Marvel's The Avengers (2012). Tony's answer, "Genius, billionaire, playboy, philanthropist," became one of the franchise's most quoted lines.
usage:
The first box is the white strip under Tony: his answer, ideally a list of four comma-separated titles that mirrors the original rhythm. The second box sits above the subtitle and defaults to Steve's "Big man in a suit of armor."; edit it to name the person or thing being challenged ("Big app with dark mode.").

The best captions keep the four-word cadence while making the answer pitiful or oddly specific. Products stripped of their one feature, players without their star teammate and people defined by a single hobby are all good targets.
ideas: Big man in a suit of armor.
Big startup with an AI label.
tired, broke, sleepy, still in debt

a regular phone with a worse charger

aka: Big Man in a Suit of Armor
